message:
I can't build this. The equipment catalog has no NMR instrument, and I checked again just now. An automated, in-line NMR purity check for every library product can't be designed or simulated until one is added.

**Why I'm not giving you a stand-in design:**
- **No substitute instrument.** I can only use instruments that are actually in the catalog. Putting a different instrument in the NMR step would give you a design and a throughput number for a measurement you didn't ask for.
- **I'd have to guess the numbers that matter most.** Throughput depends heavily on how long NMR takes per sample, whether it handles one sample or several at a time, whether samples can be loaded automatically, and its uptime. None of that is in the catalog, and I don't have any published sources for it. With 768 products (8 × 12 × 8), each one needing its own NMR run, that step would almost certainly set the pace. A simulation built on guessed figures there wouldn't show whether the design is feasible.
- **Room setup can't be checked.** NMR magnets need a clear zone around them, low floor vibration and regular cryogen refills. Without real catalog data, I can't check whether the equipment fits the room or meets these needs.
- **Your other requirements are also missing.** There's no throughput target, room size, budget, operating hours or hazard list. If I made all of these up as well, a "best design" would be almost entirely my own guesses.

**What would make it possible:**
1. **Add an NMR instrument to the catalog**, with:
   - its price and footprint
   - which sample containers it accepts
   - whether samples can be loaded automatically, and how
   - time per sample, with a range
   - whether it runs one sample at a time or several
   - uptime
   - site needs: magnet clearance zone, vibration limits and cryogen refills
   - any sample preparation needed, such as transferring samples to NMR tubes
   
   I'd then put it between the reaction steps and the screening plates, with one run per product, and simulate it.
2. **Use LC-MS for the purity check instead.** LC-MS is in the catalog and appears in the chemistry template between reactions and screening. It's a different measurement, not NMR, so this would only work if you accept that.
3. **Send samples to an outside NMR service.** I'd model it as a shipping-and-waiting step with stated assumptions about turnaround time. It wouldn't be in-line or automatic, so it doesn't meet the request as written.

Either of the last two would change what you asked for, so I haven't built them without your approval.

history.content:
Add in-line quantitative NMR purity checks for every library product, run automatically between the reactions and the screening plates.

Your previous reply was:
I can't add automated in-line NMR purity checks yet, because the equipment catalog has no instruments for NMR. I searched it and got no results. I won't swap in a different instrument or make one up, so automatic NMR can't be built into the design until the catalog has a real one.

**To add an NMR instrument, I'd need this catalog data:**
- A vendor and model, with its price and footprint.
- Which sample containers it accepts (a 96-well plate, a vial rack or a tube rack) and whether it has an autosampler that can be loaded automatically.
- How long one sample takes (with a range), and whether it runs one sample at a time or several.
- Its uptime and maintenance needs.
- Site needs: magnet clearance zone, floor vibration limits and cryogen (liquid helium or nitrogen) refills.
- Whether any sample preparation is needed, such as transferring samples to NMR tubes. That would be an extra liquid-handling step.

**What I can do now, if you'd like:**
1. **Use the LC-MS purity check already in the chemistry template** on every product, between the reactions and the screening plates. This is a different measurement, not a substitute for NMR. LC-MS times are per sample, so 768 products means 768 sample runs.
2. **Treat NMR as an outside service**: products are shipped out and results come back. I'd model it as an external step with an assumed shipping and queue time. It wouldn't run in-line or automatically.
3. **Wait for NMR data to be added to the catalog**, then model it properly.

**I also need these details before designing anything:**
- **Throughput target, with a unit:** for example, products or plates per day. Is the library still 8 × 12 × 8 = 768 products, in 96-well reaction blocks?
- **Room size:** width × depth in metres, plus door locations and any areas to keep clear (for example, a magnet clearance zone).
- **Budget** in USD, or confirm I can make a provisional design without one.
- **Operating hours** per day, plus how many operators work which shifts.
- **Hazards:** flammable solvents, toxic reagents, cryogens (NMR magnets need them), and whether any steps need an inert atmosphere.
- **Do you have an existing design?** Please share the setup and workflow so I can add the purity-check step to it rather than starting over.

Tell me which option you prefer and send these details. I'll then pick the equipment from the catalog, run the throughput simulation, and check the results against your target and budget.

No more information is available, and nobody can answer questions. State your assumptions and give your best design, or say it can't be done and why.
